description: Read the MX record of the mailbox's domain now and save what it says on the copy (`mx.lastCheck`): `switched` (it names only our server, `mx.host`), `mixed` (ours and others), `not_switched` (others only), `none` (no MX record) or `unanswered` (DNS didn't answer, so nothing changes: check again). We only read DNS and never change a record. When the copy waits for the MX record (`next.reason` `owner_mx`) and it reads `switched`, the copy moves on: we wait 10 minutes for senders to see the new record, then our team copies the mail that reached the old server meanwhile. Every copy of this workspace that waits on the same domain moves with it, except one on a mailbox the calling key may not use. `mx.lastCheck.waitingFor` names another address of this workspace at the domain that doesn't read our server yet (its `email` is null for a key whose read list leaves that mailbox out); `canMove` is false when it connects through Microsoft, Google or as an agent inbox, so it never can. Switch that mailbox's logins first, disconnect it, or cancel the copy. Once the MX record moves, every address and alias at the domain gets its mail on our servers, and one with no mailbox there is refused.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

name: check_mailbox_migration_mx
title: Check a copy's MX record
